Alka: papa said no to 9:30 on friday 😔
Alka: the show is at the school hall and ends at 8:45
Jasleen: what did you say to him
Alka: i said EVERYONE gets to stay
Jasleen: yeah he hears that all day lol
Jasleen: it gives him nothing to work with
Jasleen: give him a plan
Alka: like what
Jasleen: five of you, show ends 8:45, Meera's dad drops everyone, you text when you reach home
Alka: and if he says no again?
Jasleen: then you ask what would make him say yes. no threatening
Alka: ok. trying tonight 🙏
Jasleen: and say thank you either way

qa.q: What did Alka's papa say no to?
qa.a: Papa said no to 9:30 on Friday.

qa.q: Why is Alka feeling low at the start of the chat?
qa.a: Alka feels disappointed and maybe a little unheard since Papa said no. Alka also wants to attend the show with friends.

qa.q: What advice from Jasleen could make Alka's appeal work better?
qa.a: Giving Papa a clear plan with reasons, like who is coming and who is driving, and asking what would make him say yes. Alka should stay polite whatever he says.

qa.q: How might Alka's father see Alka's earlier answer that everyone gets to stay?
qa.a: He may see it as pressure without information, which does not help him judge whether it is safe.

grounding: A teen appeals for a later curfew, and reasons and respectful tone work better than pressure.

passage: Anand had worked out his speech while feeding the buffaloes. When his mother Disha came back from the well, he did not sulk about the mela as he had last year. "Ma, the evening aarti at the temple fair is at seven. Can I stay till the last bus at eight-thirty?" Disha kept wringing her dupatta. "Who else is going?" "Cousin Dev and two boys from school. I finished the fodder and I'll carry the phone. I'll call from the bus stand." She looked at him a long moment. "If you call, and you're back by nine, then yes. We'll see how it goes and talk again next time." Anand nodded, smiled, and did not push for more.

qa.q: Where was Anand when he prepared his request?
What does Anand want from his mother, and what in his behaviour suggests it?
qa.a: He hopes to stay for the evening aarti at the mela and wants her trust, shown by his prepared speech and the reasons he gives. He is trying not to sulk as he did last year.
His respectful tone, the concrete details about who is going and when he will call, and the fact that he finished his chores made the request easier to trust.

qa.q: How might Disha feel as she agrees?
qa.a: She may feel a little worried, yet proud that he asked properly, so a trial for one evening feels reasonable. 🙂

grounding: A teen appeals to a parent with reasons and a respectful tone, and it works better than pressure.
